physical activity and sedentary behaviour and their relationship to health.
the relationship between physical activity, screen time, overweight/obesity and health.
the relationships between physical activity, sedentary behavior and health outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence of a relationship between screen time and overweight or obesity.
while the prevalence rates of S-MVFA, HST and overweight or obesity are increasing at similar rates, the overall prevalence of overweight or obesity is higher than that of S-MVAP and HST.
there is a strong association between sedentary behaviors, physical activity and overweight/obesity, and that this relationship is not changing over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to reduce sedentary behavior in the general population, and that there is a particular need to reduce sedentariness in those who are already insufficiently physically active.
while the prevalence in S-MVPA has increased, the proportion of individuals classified as I-PVA/HST and overweight or obese has also increased over the study duration.
the prevalence of overweight or obese adults in the community is increasing and this is associated with a combination of low physical activity and high screen time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the prevalence of overweight or obesity is increasing at the same rate as screen time in the population, and that this trend is particularly evident in individuals classified as insufficiently active and high screen time.

the proportion of the adult population engaging in sufficient MVPA is increasing at the same time as the proportion engaging in high levels of sedentary behaviors and classified as overweight/obese is also increasing.
the prevalence of sufficient physical activity is increasing but not at a rate that will offset the increase in the proportion of people who are overweight or obese.
